label: rare: copy-phase input j (esp. before digit 1 / z)
explanation: Extremely sparse feature (0.024% of steps). About 60% of activation mass is on copy-phase steps whose input is the fed-back token j, typically j at original position >= 2, and the strongest cases have out_tok (and next_out) in {1, z, 2}, e.g. ...j 1 z 1.... Even so it fires on only ~1% of copy-phase j steps, so precision is very low, and adding out_tok == 1 raises precision only to ~13%. What decides which j steps fire is not captured by any per-step variable I tried. The remaining mass is scattered: late original-phase steps (t >= 6) on varied tokens such as w, v, p, b, q, the <DEL> step, and copy steps on z or p. It never fires at t < 4, at recall_idx 1, or on incorrect copies. Magnitude is highest on j followed by 1/z outputs; I did not find another magnitude modulator.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=j (+4.12), out_tok=1 (+4.01), phase=2 & in_tok=p (+3.48), orig2=n (+3.02), next_out=1 (+2.78), in_tok=j (+2.60). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-3.39), recall_idx=1 (-3.13), t=3 (-2.73), phase=2 (-2.24).
